name: Millhaven
description: A prosperous market town built along the banks of the River Alder, Millhaven serves as the commercial heart of the region. Watermills line the riverfront, their steady clatter mixing with the calls of merchants in the cobblestone square. Stone buildings with thatched roofs cluster around the central market, and the town guard keeps a visible presence at the gates. It is a place of relative safety and opportunity — the kind of town where adventurers find their first quests pinned to the notice board of the Hearthstone Tavern.

name: Millhaven Outskirts
description: The farmlands and rolling meadows surrounding Millhaven stretch out beneath a wide sky. Wheat fields sway in the breeze alongside fenced pastures dotted with sheep. The occasional farmstead sends chimney smoke curling upward, and dirt paths wind between low stone walls. Wolves have been spotted more frequently of late, and goblins from the eastern hills have grown bolder — the farmers speak of stolen livestock and strange tracks in the mud.

name: The Old Road
description: A weathered trade route that has connected the towns of the region for centuries. Ancient mile markers carved with faded runes stand at intervals along the packed-earth road, half-swallowed by creeping ivy. The road passes through open grassland and shallow valleys, offering little cover. Merchant caravans travel in groups for safety, and the roadside ditches sometimes reveal the rusted remnants of old ambushes. Bandits and opportunistic creatures have been known to prey on lone travelers.

name: Darkwood Forest
description: An ancient and sprawling forest of towering oaks and twisted elms whose canopy blocks most sunlight even at midday. The air is thick with the scent of moss and rotting leaves, and strange birdcalls echo between the trunks. Game trails crisscross the undergrowth, but few lead anywhere safe. The deeper one ventures, the older the trees become, their bark scarred with claw marks and strange symbols. Druids once tended these woods, and their abandoned stone circles still hum with faint energy on moonlit nights.

name: Goblin Caves
description: A network of natural limestone caves carved deeper by generations of goblin habitation. The entrance is a jagged maw in a hillside, half-hidden by thornbushes and marked by crude totems of bone and feather. Inside, the tunnels are low-ceilinged and slippery, lit by guttering torches jammed into cracks in the rock. The goblins have dug pit traps and strung crude alarms of tin cans and wire. The air smells of smoke, refuse, and something worse lurking in the deeper chambers.

name: Thornfield Village
description: A small, quiet village nestled in a shallow valley, surrounded by fields of barley and wildflower meadows. Thornfield has perhaps thirty families, a single tavern called The Thorny Crown, a modest temple to Chauntea, and an aging blacksmith who mostly repairs farm tools. The village elder keeps a worried eye on the hills to the east, from which goblin raids have increased. Despite its troubles, the villagers are welcoming to travelers, if cautious — strangers sometimes bring trouble as often as salvation.

name: Ruins of Aldenmere
description: The crumbling remains of a city that fell to an unknown catastrophe over three centuries ago. Broken towers claw at the sky like skeletal fingers, and collapsed walls form a maze of rubble-choked corridors open to the elements. Vegetation has reclaimed much of the stonework, but beneath the ivy and moss, faded carvings hint at Aldenmere's former grandeur. Treasure hunters and scholars come here seeking artifacts, but few return with more than scratches and nightmares. The undead stir in the deeper vaults, and something ancient watches from the old keep.

name: The Silver Mine
description: An abandoned dwarven mining operation carved into the base of the Greypeak Hills. The entrance is a reinforced timber frame leading into well-cut tunnels that descend steeply into the earth. Rusted mine carts sit on corroded tracks, and the walls still glitter with veins of unworked silver. The dwarves left decades ago after breaking into a natural cavern system that released something dangerous. The upper levels are relatively safe, but the lower shafts echo with sounds that no natural creature should make.

name: Ravenwatch Tower
description: A grim stone watchtower perched on a craggy hilltop overlooking the eastern approach to the valley. Built generations ago to guard against incursions from the Blighted Lands, the tower has changed hands many times. Currently occupied by a mysterious figure known only as the Warden, who keeps a flock of trained ravens as messengers and scouts. The tower's lower floors are fortified with arrow slits and murder holes, and its dungeons are said to hold prisoners — or worse. Gaining entry requires either an invitation or considerable force.

name: Crossroads Inn
description: A large, well-maintained coaching inn standing at the junction where the Old Road meets the northern trail to the highlands. The inn is built of sturdy oak timbers and river stone, with a broad common room warmed by two great hearths. Travelers of all kinds pass through — merchants, pilgrims, soldiers, and the occasional adventuring party. The innkeeper, a retired soldier named Kael, runs a tight establishment and tolerates no brawling. The stables can hold a dozen horses, and the rooms are clean if simple. Rumors flow as freely as the ale.

name: Whispering Marsh
description: A vast expanse of boggy wetland where thick mist clings to the surface of dark, still water. Gnarled trees draped in hanging moss rise from the mire like hunched figures, and the ground shifts treacherously between solid hummocks and deep mud. The marsh earns its name from the eerie, almost-vocal sounds that drift through the fog — the wind through hollow reeds, or perhaps something else entirely. Will-o'-wisps have been spotted leading travelers astray, and the local villagers warn of a hag who dwells somewhere in the deepest reaches.

name: Temple of the Dawn
description: A serene hilltop temple dedicated to Lathander, the Morninglord, its white marble walls catching the first light of every sunrise. The temple grounds are immaculately maintained, with gardens of golden flowers and a clear spring that locals believe has minor healing properties. A small order of clerics tends the temple and offers healing, counsel, and shelter to those in need. The high priestess, Sister Aurelia, is known for her visions — she claims the Morninglord has shown her dark times ahead and seeks worthy champions to face them.

name: Highland Pass
description: A narrow mountain trail winding through the rocky foothills of the Greypeaks, flanked by steep cliffs and loose scree. The pass is the only viable overland route to the northern territories, and its exposed switchbacks offer little shelter from the biting wind. Eagles circle overhead, and mountain goats navigate the ledges with far more confidence than any biped. Bandit ambushes are a constant threat in the narrow sections, and rockslides can block the path for days. At the highest point, a crude stone cairn marks the border between the settled lands and the wilds beyond.

name: Blighted Hollow
description: A cursed valley where no plant grows green and no bird sings. The trees are blackened and leafless, the soil is ashen grey, and a perpetual overcast hangs above as if the sky itself recoils from this place. At the center of the hollow lies the remnants of a ritual circle scorched into bare rock, surrounded by shattered obsidian pillars. Whatever happened here poisoned the land itself, and the corruption has been slowly spreading outward for years. Undead and aberrant creatures wander the blighted ground, drawn to the residual dark energy. Only the brave or the foolish venture here willingly.

name: Hermit's Grove
description: A hidden clearing deep within the Darkwood Forest, accessible only through a barely visible deer trail that even experienced trackers might miss. Ancient standing stones encircle a massive oak tree at the center, its trunk wide enough for three people to shelter inside. A druid hermit named Oakenhart has lived here for decades, tending the balance of nature in the forest. His grove is a place of peace — predators and prey drink from the same spring here without conflict. Oakenhart is reclusive but not hostile, and he possesses knowledge of the forest's secrets that no one else holds.
